pr.title: Compute jump threading opportunities in a single pass
pr.description:
The current implementation of jump threading walks MIR CFG backwards from each `SwitchInt` terminator. This PR replaces this by a single postorder traversal of MIR. In theory, we could do a full fixpoint dataflow analysis, but this has low returns as we forbid threading through a loop header.

The second commit in this PR modifies the carried state to a lighter data structure. The current implementation uses some kind of `IndexVec<ValueIndex, &[Condition]>`. This is needlessly heavy, as the state rarely ever carries more than a few `Condition`s. The first commit replaces this state with a simpler `&[Condition]`, and puts the corresponding `ValueIndex` inside `Condition`.

The three later commits are perf tweaks.

The sixth commit is the main change. Instead of carrying the goto target inside the condition, we maintain a set of conditions associated with each block, and their consequences in following blocks. Think: if this condition is fulfilled in this block, then that condition is fulfilled in that block. This makes the threading algorithm much easier to implement, without the extra bookkeeping of `ThreadingOpportunity` we had.

Later commits modify that algorithm to shrink the set of duplicated blocks. By propagating fulfilled conditions down the CFG, and trimming costly threads.

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: This PR replaces per-SwitchInt backward DFS jump-threading search with a single postorder condition-graph construction, then applies fulfilled conditions forward while deduplicating/cloning blocks and trimming costly chains. The reusable knowledge is the condition-transfer invariants: thread only non-loop-header paths, deduplicate repeated successor conditions, preserve aliasing kills and Not/Eq semantics, and never rewrite a chained target block in place when it may later need to be duplicated.
analysis.originalLogic: The pre-PR implementation was described in the source as follows: "We proceed by walking the cfg backwards starting from each `SwitchInt` terminator, looking for assignments that will turn the `SwitchInt` into a simple `Goto`." It carried a `State<ConditionSet>` mapping places to conditions, started a search from every `SwitchInt`, bounded recursion with `MAX_BACKTRACK = 5`, bounded instruction cost with `MAX_COST = 100`, and only recursed through `Goto` terminators. It recorded `ThreadingOpportunity { chain, target }` values and later applied those chains. The new phase 1 associates conditions and consequences with blocks ("we maintain a set of conditions associated with each block, and their consequences in following blocks"); phase 2 propagates fulfilled conditions forward and applies `Goto`/`Chain` effects, cloning blocks only when needed.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: No confirmed semantic miscompile of the final PR is established. The historically risky transformation inside chain application was rewriting the chained successor block in place instead of cloning a block for the pair `(target, condition)`. The patch explicitly warns: "We may be tempted to modify `target` in-place to avoid a clone. This is wrong. We may still have edges from other blocks to `target` that have not been created yet. For instance because we may be threading an edge coming from `bb`, or `target` may be a block duplicate for which we may still create predecessors." The regression test adds: "One version of the implementation was buggy and mutated a bb that would be duplicated later." Therefore the incorrect transformation to target in a differential test is: when a condition is chained into `target`, mutate `target`'s terminator/state directly rather than creating or reusing a duplicate keyed by `(target, condition)`. The final algorithm uses the duplicate cache and leaves the original target intact.
analysis.inputDomain: Valid MIR immediately before the `JumpThreading` pass, for non-cleanup basic blocks. The interesting inputs contain a `SwitchInt` whose discriminant can be proven constant on some incoming path, including conditions derived from `if`, `match`, `?`, `Option`/enum discriminants, aggregate constants and projections, copies, `assume`, unary `Not`, and `Eq`/`Ne` comparisons. Conditions may be chained across several blocks; the same block may fulfill multiple conditions; a switch may have repeated successor blocks. The pass deliberately does not thread through a block in `maybe_loop_headers`. It uses `MAX_COST = 100` and `MAX_PLACES = 100`. For using outgoing branch facts, the code says: "Only support the case where there are no duplicated outgoing edges." For a general switch it says: "We have a general switch and we cannot express `discr != value0 && discr != value1`, so we only generate equality predicates." A concrete pair for a focused agent: (A) `let a = 2; if a == 2 { 0 } else { 1 }`; (B) `let a = 2; let b = a; if b == 2 { 0 } else { 1 }`, where B adds only the copy-based condition transfer. The historical test `two_reads` is the stronger form: `let a = 2; let b = a; let c = a; if c == 2 { 0 } else { 1 }`.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` branch has a discriminant place whose value is fixed or constrained on an incoming edge, and the condition can be propagated backward through the block's statements to a constant assignment, copy, aggregate/discriminant projection, `Not`, or comparison, then forward along successor edges without crossing a loop header. Multiple fulfilled conditions can share the same block, and repeated successor blocks must be deduplicated before registering `Chain` edges.
preconditions: The block is not a cleanup block; cleanup blocks are skipped when building entry states.
The relevant terminator is `SwitchInt` and its discriminant maps through value_analysis to a `ValueIndex`; otherwise no condition is generated.
Do not thread through `maybe_loop_headers`; the pass must avoid creating irreducible control flow.
For the static-if case, generate both `discr == value -> then` and `discr != value -> else`; for a general switch, generate only equality predicates.

When using outgoing edges to fulfill existing conditions, require distinct switch targets (`targets.is_distinct()`); for a `Ne` condition, all branch constants must be checked against `targets.all_values()` before using the otherwise edge.
Deduplicate repeated successors and duplicate `EdgeEffect::Chain` entries for the same condition.
A statement that mutates or partially assigns a place must flood/remove conditions on aliasing places using `for_each_aliasing_place` and `TrackElem`.
Costs are bounded by `MAX_COST = 100`; cyclic costs start at `MAX_COST` and use saturating addition, and costly chains are removed after simplification.
When applying `Chain`, clone or reuse a duplicate keyed by `(target, condition)`; never mutate the original target block in place.
pitfalls: Mutating a chained target block in place can corrupt another path that later needs the unmodified target or a duplicate of it; the source explicitly calls this "wrong."
Threading across a loop header can create irreducible control flow; skip loop headers and never include them in a chain.
A block may list the same successor several times; without deduplication the condition graph records duplicate targets/edges and can unbalance predecessor counting.
A general `SwitchInt` cannot express `discr != v0 && discr != v1`; do not synthesize a negative condition for the otherwise edge unless all branch values have been accounted for.
Transferring conditions through `Not` must invert the compared value in the correct layout; issue #131195 is guarded by tests because `!a == b` must not be rewritten as `a != b` incorrectly.
Do not reason through inline asm; the implementation clears active conditions for `InlineAsm`.
`Assert` may be a no-op at codegen time, so it is treated as not modifying memory.
The simplification pass must count only reachable incoming edges, deduplicate fulfilled targets, and update predecessor counts after a `Goto` removes other successors.

Fulfilling a condition on a branch edge does not mean the condition is fulfilled in the current block when some targets go elsewhere; only mark the existing condition fulfilled if all of its targets are covered, otherwise create a new condition index.
Do not treat the PR as a confirmed semantic bug fix: the description is about replacing a heavy backward search with a single traversal and later "perf tweaks"/duplication shrinking.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the existing `tests/mir-opt/jump_threading.rs` harness with `// EMIT_MIR jump_threading.<function>.JumpThreading.diff` and `CHECK-LABEL`/`CHECK`/`CHECK-NOT`/`CHECK-NEXT` assertions; the harness emits both panic-abort and panic-unwind diffs, so update both. For the basic trigger, use `two_reads` and assert that the `switchInt(move [[eq]])` becomes `goto -> bb1` while `bb1` still returns 0 and `bb2` returns 1. For copy/aggregate transfer, use `aggregate`, `aggregate_copy`, `bitwise_not`, and `logical_not`; the test comments say \"Verify that we can thread jumps when we assign from an aggregate constant\" and \"Verify that jump threading succeeds seeing through copies of aggregates.\" For the chain-application regression, add a nested `match` like `chained_conditions` with `Option<String>`, string guards, and an enum `BacktraceStyle`; the comment says \"Verify that we correctly handle threading multiple conditions on the same bb\" and \"One version of the implementation was buggy and mutated a bb that would be duplicated later.\" Include multiple-match, disappearing-block, custom-discriminant, renumbered-block, duplicate-chain, and too-complex cases to cover repeated successors, block reuse, and cost trimming. For differential testing, keep source behavior identical and vary only the condition-transfer shape (direct constant vs through a copy or chained block), then compare MIR before/after `JumpThreading` for the expected `goto`/cloned-block result. No compiler execution is claimed here; these are source-backed test-design recommendations.
evidence: One version of the implementation was buggy and mutated a bb that would be duplicated later.
Verify that we can thread jumps when we assign from an aggregate constant.
Verify that jump threading succeeds seeing through copies of aggregates.
Assertions can be no-op at codegen time, so treat them as such.
Do not thread through loop headers.
A given block may have several times the same successor.
